exposure: COVID-19 infection during the first wave of the pandemic (May 2020-Feb 2021)
COVID-19 infection during the second wave of the pandemic (Mar 2021-Oct 2021)
COVID-19 infection during the third wave of the pandemic (Nov 2021-Feb 2022)
outcome: Clinical presentations (asymptomatic, mild, moderate, severe COVID-19 disease)
Pregnancy outcomes (cesarean section rate, preterm delivery rate, stillbirths)
cohort: 306 pregnant women who tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 infection and were admitted to a referral hospital in Jamshedpur, India.
finding: The severity of COVID-19 disease and maternal mortality were significantly higher during the second wave, while the incidence of stillbirths was highest during the third wave of the pandemic.
mod_finding: The second wave of the pandemic witnessed a higher rate of cesarean sections compared to the first and third waves.
